_note: Traditions with no single founder (Kevin, 2026-11-23, approved with his edit): one `theme` row per tradition in a 'Religions and traditions' group, the same ids in every timeline (seams). The row's start is the mainstream scholarly date (the headline); the other scholarly dates are date claims, drawn as the faded range; the most extreme claim is never the headline. A 'roots' claim dates the tradition it grew out of, with a note. Events: dated texts, councils, schools and reforms, each placed in the timeline whose range holds it; `places` puts an event on the row of the place where it happened too (Kevin, 2026-11-23: "the associated event in whatever region or location it came from"), where the timeline has that row; `shared` adds a tradition row to an event that is already in a timeline. Years are stored years (negative = BCE, no year 0). Every claim quotes its article; pipelines/common/traditions.py --check verifies each quote against the Wikipedia dump. PILOT: 4 traditions from 4 regions. Claims may cite `web_sources` (scholarly pages, cached in $TIMELINES_DATA/traditions-sources/ by traditions.py --cache and checked the same way). An event may carry `categories`: pinned by this list (applied after Kevin's reviewed overrides, before the keyword classifier, with the evidence "pinned: pipelines/common/traditions.json").
